newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone journalists protest over press bill.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone journalists protest over press bill.

text.p: Around 100 members of the Sierra Leone Association of Journalists picketed parliament on Tuesday to protest against a bill they say threatens to shut down newspapers and radio stations.

Parliament last week passed the Newspaper Act, the first part of a press bill which reporters say is restrictive. The second part of the bill, the Media Practitioner Act, is currently before parliament in the capital Freetown.
"The Press Bill is fatal to human rights and democracy in Sierra Leone," read the placard of one of the group of protesting editors, broadcasters and newspaper reporters.
The bill would give the government the right to decide who can work as a journalist in Sierra Leone, as well as imposing strict conditions on newspapers and radio stations.
Even if passed by parliament, the bill would have to be ratified by President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, whose election in 1996 ended four years of army rule in the war-ravaged West African country.
